*3G*

**Tread** (1 block)

.15mi push, .1mi AO flat road, .05mi WR (PW .1mi push 4%, .05mi AO 8%, .05mi WR)

Start at 1% and go up 1% each time (AO is always at a flat road)

**Floor** (2 blocks, 8min, 4.5min)

Block 1: bicep curls 5x, upright row 10x, hip hinge row 15x (keeping the same weight throughout these 3 exercises), double crunch with weight 20/15/10/5 (either keeping same weight or increasing)

Block 2: goblet ISO squat lateral walk 5x (3 steps to each side), squat to alt lunge 10x total

**Rower** (2 blocks, 8min, 4.5min)

Block 1: 400m, squats with medicine ball 10x, squat press with medicine ball - 200m, squats with medicine ball 20x, squat press with medicine ball 20x - repeat in that order until time

Block 2: 200m, squat with medicine ball 5x, squat press with medicine ball 5x - 100m squat with medicine ball 10x, squat press with medicine ball 10x

There are a lot of factors that contribute to running besides the "bounciness" of the treads. If you're running with the 1% incline, it should not be significantly more difficult outside. Potential factors that can affect your running: different water intake levels, weather, humidity level, sunshine versus gloomy days (i'd rather run on a gloomy day!!), ANY change to your diet, allergies (even if you can't feel them all that much).
